corrected_statement: By the month-12 program gate, no positive real-world calibration claim (that coverage is near the nominal 80% rather than 60–70%) is statistically supportable. Separating 80% from 60% coverage (one-sided α = 0.05, power 0.8) first becomes possible at n = 35 (reject if ≤ 23 covered) and holds for every n ≥ 38 (n = 37 falls short). Separating 80% from 70% needs n = 116 (every n ≥ 127). Expected evidence: FY2026 per-site public forecasts for 14 reporting sites (11 gold, 3 copper; Barrick_Q2_2026_Mine_Stats.xlsx QTD rows 5–29) in one period. With 3–4 metrics each that is 42–56 outcomes, and an equicorrelation ρ = 0.1–0.5 gives n_eff ≈ 2–9. The GATE-TOUCH-05 hindcast and the two forward quarters (BD-209, 'inside the tenancy', line 7925) exist only if site data arrives (P ≈ 0.29, §34.4); if they do, 4–8 scored hindcast quarters and P(both forward quarters covered | calibrated 0.8) = 0.64 add little. Gross miscalibration can still be detected at small n: ≤ 4 covered of n_eff ≈ 9 rejects 0.8 (P = 0.020). Correction to the F7 aside: F7 (line 7203) describes a '90%' interval, and P(≤ 4 of 8 covered | 0.9) = 0.005, so F7's story is strong evidence of miscalibration, not borderline (0.056 applies only to an 80% interval). The plan's `uncalibrated` default and small-sample caveat (lines 7394, 4123, 7482) are consistent with this; GB-38's assumption that a pre-registered scored forecast is persuasive (line 7366, not 7365) rests on an n_eff of a few.

corrected_statement: GATE-HELM-02 ('recovers the closed-form EVSI of GB-29-type discrete problems to within 2·SE across 100 seeds', line 4766; BD-227) does not say which reading applies. Every seed within 2·SE passes an unbiased estimator with probability 0.9545¹⁰⁰ = 0.0095. The mean of 100 seeds within 2·SE_mean passes with 0.9545 per problem. At least 90 of 100 seeds within 2·SE passes with 0.994. 'Problems' is plural: over K problems the mean reading passes an unbiased estimator with probability 0.9545^K (0.79 at K = 5, 0.63 at K = 10). P03's proposed fix (mean test AND ≥ 90/100 per problem) gives 0.949^K (0.77 at K = 5, 0.59 at K = 10), so the fix also needs multiplicity control, for example a Bonferroni-adjusted z or a χ² test of the K standardised deviations. No Monte Carlo VOI estimator exists at HEAD: fmine-decide (src/lib.rs line 73) calls the closed-form compute_evsi (crates/fmine-numerics/src/voi.rs line 62), which uses no seeds, yet BD-227 ('VOI estimator vs closed-form EVSI') is closed.

corrected_statement: GATE-PLUMB-E5 ('false alarms ≤ α', line 1021) and GATE-CORE-02 (line 1575) give neither the number of null runs nor the test. At the plan's simulated false-alarm rate of 3.8% (§10.4 line 951), a one-sided 95% Clopper–Pearson upper bound ≤ 0.05 needs roughly 900–1,000 null runs (N = 1,000 gives 0.0495; N = 600 gives 0.054; N = 200 gives 0.071). Tested as a point estimate, a monitor at exactly α passes 54–58% of the time. KILL-PLUMB-6 (line 1026) counts observed false alarms ('more than 1 per site per quarter') summed over the M monitor streams. At about 30 polygons a quarter, each CUSUM stream needs ARL₀ ≥ 30·M polygons for an expected budget of 1 per quarter (600 at M = 20). Because the kill counts observed alarms, an expected rate of exactly 1 per quarter still fires it in 26% of quarters (Poisson); holding per-quarter kill risk to 5% needs an expected rate ≤ 0.36, i.e. ARL₀ ≥ ≈ 85·M. The plan gives no M, CUSUM h or ARL₀.
